key_insight: Bi-FORK learns bifurcating systems where one input can lead to multiple valid outcomes, instead of forcing a single prediction. It provides a generative way to model symmetry-breaking behavior in high-dimensional physics problems.
problem_solved: Most learned physical surrogates assume a one-to-one mapping from input to output, which breaks down in bifurcation settings. This paper addresses the challenge of representing and generating multiple equally valid solution trajectories for the same initial condition.
method: Introduces Bi-FORK, a generative framework for one-to-many solution maps in high-dimensional dynamical systems.
Models complete trajectories through bifurcation events rather than predicting a single deterministic path.
Learns to capture symmetry-breaking behavior and the resulting diverse valid outcomes from the same input.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners working on scientific machine learning, since many real-world systems are inherently multimodal and non-unique. Bi-FORK expands surrogate modeling beyond deterministic predictions, enabling more faithful simulation of complex physical processes.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram showing a single input splitting into multiple valid trajectories at a bifurcation point
Trajectory plot with branched paths illustrating alternative outcomes
Schematic of symmetry-breaking in a physical system such as buckling or fluid flow
Icon set comparing deterministic prediction vs generative one-to-many modeling
paper_title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
paper_authors: Anna Zimmel, Fleur Hendriks, Markus Holzleitner, Florian Sestak, Martin Weichselbaumer
